Summary  
Data source overview: The blog post summarizes results from the 2016 AI Impacts expert survey of 352 machine-learning researchers. It reports forecast distributions for human-level machine intelligence (HLMI), large framing effects on those forecasts, and strong but varied concern among researchers about misaligned AI risks similar to Stuart Russell’s alignment argument. The post contains no detailed technical mitigation proposals but does reveal researchers’ support for increasing safety work and shows methodological levers (survey framing, clearer definitions) that influence readiness planning.  

Inference strategy justification: When explicit interventions were absent, I applied the prompt’s “moderate inference” allowance to derive three interventions that an AI-safety analyst would naturally extract from the evidence presented: (1) increase AI-safety research funding (explicitly desired by respondents), (2) run multi-framing surveys to reduce timeline uncertainty, and (3) refine HLMI definitions to curb framing errors. All other nodes are direct quotations or close paraphrases of the post.  

Extraction completeness explanation: All causal-interventional pathways that the text implies were captured:  
1. Misalignment-driven catastrophic risk → growing researcher recognition → community support → increased safety research funding.  
2. Preparedness shortfall risk from inaccurate timelines → forecast variation → framing effects → methodological interventions (multi-framing surveys, clearer definitions).  
All nodes inter-connect through shared “support for increasing safety research”, forming a single fabric. No isolated nodes remain.  

Key limitations:  
• The source is qualitative; all edge confidences above “medium” would be unwarranted.  
• Interventions are high-level and policy-oriented, so lifecycle stage 6 (“Other”) was used.  
• The Russell quote was the only technical causal mechanism, so deeper mechanistic nodes could not be extracted.  

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[82] – Reasonably high; JSON validated, pathways connected, moderate inference documented. Prompts could improve by providing explicit mapping examples for policy-level interventions to lifecycle codes and by clarifying preferred edge directions when the risk node is an effect of preceding causes.
